newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan surplus increase would boost yen more--Kato.
newsitem.headline: Japan surplus increase would boost yen more--Kato.

text.p: The yen would strengthen further if Japan's trade surplus were to increase, Koichi Kato, secretary-general of Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), told Reuters in an interview on Thursday.
"If it (Japanese trade surplus) were to rise substantially, then the yen rate would rise," Kato said.
But he added that it was important not to overreact to short-term movements in the foreign exchange market.

Kato said Japanese exports had decreased following the yen's rise to a record high of around 79 yen to the dollar in April of 1995, but that Tokyo's trade surplus had started to rise as the yen fell to around 127 yen to the dollar earlier this year.
"The function of foreign exchange rates in balancing trade is working," he said.
Kato, who plays a key role in formulating LDP policies, said it was important that exchange rates stabilise but did not comment on what level was appropriate for the dollar/yen rate.
Kato said the recovery of the Japanese economy was gaining strength, centring around private demand.

He added that the recovery would be able to overcome the negative effects of fiscal consolidation measures, including spending cuts laid out in a government plan to reform the nation's debt-ridden finances. -- George Nishiyama, Tokyo Policy Desk +81-3-5473-3710
